Assign cells to paths from lineage weights

Source: R/assign_paths.R
assign_paths.Rd

assign_paths() turns the lineage weights and pseudotimes of a trajectory tool, one column per lineage as slingshot and tradeSeq give them, into what scMaSigPro needs: one pseudotime value and one path label per cell. Cells on every lineage are labelled as the root, and cells on some of the lineages get the names of those lineages joined by shared_sep: the root and link paths that sc.restruct() takes.

assign_paths(
  pseudotime,
  weights,
  min_weight = 0.5,
  root_label = "root",
  shared_sep = "_links_",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

pseudotime

The pseudotime of each cell: a numeric matrix with the row and column names of weights, such as slingshot::slingPseudotime(); or, for a pseudotime that every lineage shares, as Monocle3 gives it, a numeric vector with one value per row of weights, in that order or named by cell.

weights

A matrix or data frame of non-negative weights with one row per cell, named by cell, and one column per lineage, named by lineage and at least two of them, such as slingshot::slingCurveWeights(), the cell weights of tradeSeq or the result of paths_from_graph().

min_weight

A single positive number: a cell is on a lineage when its weight there is at least min_weight and its pseudotime there is a finite number. (Default is 0.5)

root_label

The path label of the cells on every lineage. (Default is "root")

shared_sep

The separator of the lineage names in the label of the cells on some but not all lineages; pass it to sc.restruct() as link_sep. (Default is "links", the default of sc.restruct())

verbose

Print a message when cells are left out. (Default is TRUE)

Value

A data frame with one row per cell that is on at least one lineage, in the order of the rows of weights and named by cell, and two columns: Pseudotime (numeric) and Path (character). Pass it to create_scmp() as cell_data with ptime_col = "Pseudotime" and path_col = "Path", or add its columns to the colData() of a SingleCellExperiment with the same cells for as_scmp(), whose default column names they are.

Details

Each cell is placed on the lineages where its weight is at least min_weight and its pseudotime is known. A cell on one lineage gets the name of that lineage as its path, a cell on every lineage gets root_label, and a cell on two or more lineages but not all of them gets the names of those lineages, in the order of the columns of weights, joined by shared_sep. A cell on no lineage is left out. The pseudotime of a cell is the mean of its pseudotimes on its lineages, or its value when pseudotime is a vector.

The weights are compared with min_weight as they are given. Curve weights of slingshot are close to 1 on every lineage for the cells of the root; for weights that sum to 1 in each cell, as with slingCurveWeights(as.probs = TRUE), use a min_weight below 1 / (number of lineages) or the root cells are left out. Soft weights can place a few cells on a set of lineages that share no segment of the trajectory beyond the root, such as two of three lineages that split at the root; their label is built the same way, so relabel or remove them before sc.restruct() if they are not a link.

Input contract

scMaSigPro needs one pseudotime value and one path label per cell, and nothing else from the tool that inferred the trajectory. create_scmp() takes them as a data frame named by cell, such as the result of assign_paths(), and as_scmp() as two colData() columns of a SingleCellExperiment. Code outside this package that reads a trajectory, such as a companion package for Monocle3 objects or an interactive branch selector, returns that data frame, or the R code that builds it with paths_from_graph() and assign_paths(). Its path labels follow the rules in Details, so that sc.restruct() can rebuild the paths that share a root.

See also

paths_from_graph() for weights from a trajectory graph; sc.restruct() for the root and link paths.

Author

Priyansh Srivastava spriyansh29@gmail.com

Examples

# Three lineages: cells 1 and 2 are on all of them, cell 3 on A and B
weights <- matrix(
    c(
        1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0,
        1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0,
        1, 0.9, 0.2, 0, 0, 1
    ),
    ncol = 3,
    dimnames = list(paste0("cell", 1:6), c("A", "B", "C"))
)
pseudotime <- c(0.1, 0.5, 1.2, 2.1, 2.3, 1.8)
assign_paths(pseudotime, weights)
#>       Pseudotime      Path
#> cell1        0.1      root
#> cell2        0.5      root
#> cell3        1.2 A_links_B
#> cell4        2.1         A
#> cell5        2.3         B
#> cell6        1.8         C

# A pseudotime for each lineage, as slingshot gives it
pseudotime <- cbind(A = pseudotime, B = pseudotime + 0.1, C = pseudotime)
rownames(pseudotime) <- rownames(weights)
assign_paths(pseudotime, weights, shared_sep = "|")
#>       Pseudotime Path
#> cell1  0.1333333 root
#> cell2  0.5333333 root
#> cell3  1.2500000  A|B
#> cell4  2.1000000    A
#> cell5  2.4000000    B
#> cell6  1.8000000    C
